title: Regional, Colloquial, and Written Norms
summary: Navigate variation between Brazilian regions, everyday speech, educated usage, and the written standard.

sections.heading: Variation is not error by itself
sections.body: Brazilian Portuguese varies by region, class, age, context, and medium. Advanced learners need to identify what is regional or colloquial and choose appropriately for the situation.

examples.note: common in some regions; nonstandard agreement in formal writing

sections.heading: Spoken grammar vs written norm
sections.body: Speech often uses structures that formal writing avoids, such as subject pronouns as objects, simplified agreement in fast speech, and sentence fragments. These are part of real usage but must be controlled by register.

sections.heading: Lexical regionalisms
sections.body: Different regions may prefer different words for everyday items, foods, or transport. Prefer widely understood Brazilian terms in learner materials unless teaching regional awareness.

examples.en: train; also 'thing' in parts of Minas Gerais

keyPoints: Advanced competence includes recognizing variation and controlling register.
Colloquial does not automatically mean wrong, but it may be inappropriate in formal writing.
Use widely understood Brazilian forms for national communication.
Avoid stigmatized agreement patterns in careful speech and writing.

commonMistakes.wrong: If Brazilians say it, it is always safe in formal writing.
commonMistakes.right: Spoken forms may be natural but register-limited.
Você vai is the safest national learner form.
commonMistakes.note: Tu usage is regional and agreement varies.

commonMistakes.wrong: Eu vi ela in an academic essay.
commonMistakes.right: Eu a vi / Vi-a in formal contexts.
commonMistakes.note: Use standard object pronouns or recast the sentence.
